NVDA.rationale: NVIDIA exhibits exceptional fundamental health: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $57.01B with 22% QoQ growth, 52.4% net margins, 69.8% gross margins, 86.5% ROE, and minimal debt ($8.47B vs $118.9B equity). Operating cash flow of $23.75B in the latest quarter demonstrates massive cash generation. The company dominates AI accelerators with ~80-92% market share and benefits from a $1 trillion committed order pipeline through 2027. However, several factors temper the score: (1) Valuation is elevated — P/E of 59.9x sits near the top of its 43-63.5x 12-month range, and P/B of 51.8x is also near highs, suggesting the market is paying a premium vs recent history; (2) China market is effectively foreclosed per the 10-K, with 0% official data center GPU share, benefiting competitors; (3) Custom silicon from hyperscalers (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom ASICs) represents a growing structural threat, with NVIDIA's share declining from 87% peak in 2024 to 75-80%; (4) Rising 10-year yields (4.41%) and elevated oil ($98/bbl) create macro headwinds for high-multiple stocks. The near-term catalyst is the May 20 Q1 FY2027 earnings report, with management guiding $78B revenue (77% YoY growth) and analysts expecting a beat. Goldman Sachs recently raised estimates by 12%. This credible near-term event provides a modest positive modifier. Net: excellent business quality and trajectory, but valuation near the top of its range and competitive/geopolitical headwinds cap the score at mildly attractive.

NVIDIA holds ~80% of the AI accelerator market by revenue with $193.7B in FY2026 data center sales. NVIDIA's share peaked in 2024 at 87% and is slowly giving ground to custom silicon (Broadcom, Google, AWS).

As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market, and our effective foreclosure from the China market helped our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide.

Goldman Sachs raised Nvidia's revenue and earnings estimates by roughly 12%, suggesting the company's $1 trillion AI revenue target across 2025-2027 may be conservative. The analyst expects a beat-and-raise quarter with Q1 revenue of $80.05B (vs. $78.30B consensus).
Nvidia will report Q1 earnings on May 20 with analysts expecting strong results ($78.8B revenue, $1.77 EPS).
